advisories.trigger: AnyIO process pool executes code producing enough stderr to fill its undrained pipe.
advisories.route: Pinned AnyIO 4.14.2 equals the first patched release; process-pool trigger therefore need not be disproved for this version conclusion.
advisories.import_status: Not freshly observed; distribution installation is independently retained.
advisories.unknown: No proof about arbitrary older AnyIO environments.

advisories.trigger: AnyIO connect_tcp/TLSStream.wrap handles a non-ASCII hostname, with an attacker able to redirect the connection and provide a certificate valid for the differently encoded name.
advisories.route: Pinned AnyIO 4.14.2 equals the first patched release. The configured provider endpoints are additionally fixed ASCII hostnames; that is secondary source evidence, not the basis of the fixed-version result.
advisories.import_status: Not freshly observed; distribution installation is independently retained.
advisories.unknown: No proof about arbitrary older AnyIO environments or different endpoint configurations.

advisories.trigger: Attacker-controlled fileids reach NKJPCorpusReader header/raw/words/sents/tagged_words and escape the corpus root.
advisories.route: NLTK 3.9.1 contains the NKJP reader methods. The selected official LLM partition and LLM scoring route pass task/answer text to judge templates, not corpus-reader fileids. Official partition imports ROUGE; ROUGE imports NLTK eagerly, so import cannot be described as absent. The default RougeScorer uses rouge1 and use_stemmer=False; the selected LLM dispatch does not invoke the alternative ROUGE partition helper.
advisories.import_status: Import is required by inspected official/ROUGE source and covered by retained complete-module import evidence; no new dynamic observation.
advisories.unknown: Source-level route applicability only. This is not an exploit probe or a claim that all NLTK paths, imports, unsupported algorithms or later capability changes are safe.

advisories.trigger: An attacker-influenced resource URL reaches nltk.data.load/find, with encoded traversal decoded after path checks and used for a local file open.
advisories.route: The retained NLTK 3.9.1 source contains the resource loader and URL-to-path behavior. The fixed LLM partition/scoring call path does not pass task/answer strings to NLTK load/find or request NLTK corpora/downloads. NLTK import alone is insufficient to trigger this advisory.
advisories.import_status: Same real eager import boundary as the NKJP row; no new dynamic observation.
advisories.unknown: The advisory references later pathsec behavior; this review retains the maintainer affected-version range without asserting every later-described security API exists in 3.9.1. No whole-library exploitability clearance.

advisories.trigger: A TLS verifier trusts an affected emSign root chain; an on-path attacker possesses a compromised eMudhra intermediate key and presents a forged certificate.
advisories.route: Worker SDK constructors are replaced with an httpx AsyncClient using make_transport and trust_env=False. That custom transport exchanges bounded request descriptions with the host instead of performing provider TLS. The host RawHTTPTransport creates stdlib http.client.HTTPSConnection; inspected source does not load the worker Certifi bundle into that connection. Therefore installation of this CPU Certifi version does not show that its CA bundle verifies actual provider traffic.
advisories.import_status: Installed affected version is proven by retained manifest. Import and trust-store use were not freshly observed.
advisories.unknown: Host default trust-store contents, SSL environment/configuration and whether the same emSign trust chain remains accepted by host TLS are unassessed. Overall TLS applicability remains unknown; do not mark this advisory globally cleared.

advisories.trigger: On Windows, an attacker-controlled wheel namespace_packages.txt reaches the legacy Wheel.install_as_egg conversion path with a drive-qualified namespace path, producing a fixed-content __init__.py outside the requested egg directory.
advisories.route: Setuptools 79.0.1 contains the legacy installation functions, but the pinned evaluator runtime is Linux/amd64. The permitted route runs preinstalled official partition/scoring and does not install wheels or invoke this legacy installer. Both the advisory Windows prerequisite and installation operation are absent from this exact route.
advisories.import_status: Installed version proven; whether Setuptools is incidentally imported is not established and is not the trigger distinction.
advisories.unknown: No clearance for the Windows host, dependency building/installing, future arbitrary execution, or a different platform/installer route.

Certifi_version_provenance.qualification: The original external report labels retained global-alert version fields as maintainer fields. This supplement identifies their actual provenance and preserves both sources. The maintainer page says patched2026.10.18; global metadata says2026.10.19. Installed2025.8.3 is affected under either. No package version is changed and neither source discrepancy resolves host TLS trust.
